title: SecOps-NG Detection Pointer
description: A pointer to an upstream Sigma detection rule. SecOps-NG does NOT fork or re-author Sigma; we reference rules by ID + repo + commit pin and overlay metadata that joins the rule to the playbook, control, and telemetry layers via the shared `stable_id` shape defined by the playbook schema.

stable_id.description: SecOps-NG stable identifier for this detection. Namespace convention: `detection.<slug>@v<semver>` — for example `detection.powershell_encoded_cmd@v1`. Same lexical shape as the playbook schema's stable_id so any layer can cross-reference any other.

content_version.description: Semantic version of this detection content artifact (independent of upstream Sigma versioning).

maturity.description: Content maturity tier. `draft` and `experimental` are not compiled by default in production targets.

title.description: Human-readable label. Mirrors the upstream Sigma title for findability; not authoritative.

summary.description: One-paragraph operator-facing summary of what the upstream rule detects and why we reference it.

sigma.description: Upstream Sigma rule pointer. We do not duplicate the rule body; consumers MUST resolve via repo + rule_id.

rule_id.description: Upstream Sigma rule UUID (the `id:` field in the rule YAML).

repo.description: Git URL of the upstream Sigma rule repository (e.g. https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma).

path.description: Path to the rule file inside the repo, e.g. rules/windows/process_creation/proc_creation_win_powershell_encoded_b64.yml.

commit.description: Commit SHA pin. Recommended for reproducibility. If omitted, the rule is tracked at the repo's default branch (volatile).

tags.description: Mirror of upstream Sigma tags relevant for routing (e.g. attack.t1059, tlp.amber).

logsource.description: Operator-facing summary of the Sigma logsource block, so consumers can route without fetching the rule.

severity.description: Operator-facing severity overlay. Independent of upstream Sigma `level` so a community can re-prioritise without forking the rule.

control_refs.description: Stable IDs of controls this detection contributes evidence to. Joins to control.schema.json#stable_id.

telemetry_refs.description: Stable IDs of telemetry bindings whose payloads this detection consumes. Joins to telemetry.schema.json#stable_id.

playbook_refs.description: Playbooks (and optionally specific CACAO step names) that fire on this detection.

step_id.description: Optional CACAO step name within the playbook (e.g. enrich_host_context).

maintainer.description: Email, handle, or working-group name responsible for keeping the pointer current.

sources.description: Free-form provenance pointers — upstream rule lineage, advisories, threat reports — that motivated this pointer. Plain text only; no internal infra references.

stable_id.description: SecOps-NG stable identifier (shared shape across all content-model layers). Format: `<namespace>.<slug>@v<semver>`.
